# PR #4557: Patch: the fuzz monitor fails a game in which a target drawn at random is one its card could not have chosen by hand

Closes #4540

## What changed

The fuzz monitor now has a check for targeting: every `target` pick must be one its source card may aim at. It is **I22**, not the plan's I21, because the maintainer's comment says #4508 takes I21. A pick is unlawful when it names:
- a Dormant card, from any source or none (R1839000);
- a face-up Evasive card in play, from a Spell or a Field Spell (R4353002);
- a face-up card Immune to Spells, from a Spell (R450).

The check reads zones, `slumber`, face-down state and layered keywords itself (`AuraTable`). It never calls `restrictions`, `targeting` or `targeting_point`.

It runs in three places:
- **Random draws.** `testkit/seams.rs` gains a thread-local record (`TargetDraw`, `TargetDrawBy`, `start_target_draws`, `take_target_draws`, `record_target_draw`, and `clear_seams` clears it). The engine adds to it at six sites, each one call compiled only under `testkit`:
  - `prompts::answer_at_random`;
  - both branches of `play_steps::ask_repeat_targets` (Echo repeats and a cast's choices);
  - both branches of `cry_trigger::ask_targets`;
  - `play_choices::with_drawn_target_picks`.

  The monitor's `before` opens the record and `after` judges each draw on the state it was drawn on. Outside that window nothing is kept, so `cargo jackioh gate` and AI search keep no states.
- **Listings and prompts.** `hidden` judges every `target` pick of each seat's listed plays and activations, and every option of an open `target` prompt.
- **Duos.** `DuosInvariantMonitor::after` takes the draws before the per-duel `after`s run. It files each draw under its duel by matching the state's seed (`duos_duel_seed`).

A random pick made by an effect ("a random enemy") is not targeting and is never recorded (R4353002). Only `target`-kind picks are recorded, so a Spell's random Tribute of its own Evasive unit stays lawful.

The docs now say I22 is in the monitor: the header of `invariants.rs`, `testkit/mod.rs`, the engine README, and `fuzz.rs`, `main.rs` and the `fuzz` row of `crates/tools/README.md`. No spec change, because no new rule is decided.

## Testing
- `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test rules i22`: 13 passed. They cover:
  - one bad pick of each kind, flagged with the right ruling and draw kind;
  - a Unit, Trap, Field Trap or Animated source aiming at an Evasive card, which is clean;
  - lawful picks: a bare unit, a hero, a card in hand, a face-down card;
  - the record window, and an effect's random pick, which is not judged;
  - real draws at every site, under a random cast and under a Mayor;
  - a listed play and activation retargeted at an Evasive unit (flagged; a Unit's is not);
  - an open prompt given one extra unlawful option.
- New Duos unit test `i22_a_duos_draw_is_judged_under_the_duel_it_was_drawn_in` passes.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit` (whole crate): all green (3028, 815, 671, 254 and others).
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools` (619 passed, 24 ignored, plus the smaller binaries) and `cargo test -p jackioh-cards` (10235 and 1238 passed), both with the engine's testkit: green.
- I switched off each of the six record sites in turn: every one makes an `i22` test fail.
- `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200`: 200 passed, 0 invariant violations (131 s while other builds ran; a later run took 57 s).
- `cargo jackioh fuzz --duos --seeds 50`: 0 failed, 73 s.
- A temporary instrumented build (reverted; the file matches its saved copy) measured the cost over 200 seeds. I22 judged 62 random draws, 10,690 listings and 45 open `target` prompts, taking 0.07 s in total of a 57 s wave, so there is no measurable slowdown.
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance statics_the_pure_crates_hold_only_the_statics_rule_4_allows` passed, with `RULE_4_STATICS` unchanged.
- `cargo jackioh spec check`: ok. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --all-targets -- -D warnings`, the same clippy without testkit, and `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

## Decisions the issue did not settle
- **Number I22, not I21.** I followed the approval comment. The docs say "I1–I20 and I22". The header says "twenty-one checks, I1–I20 and I22 (#4508 holds I21's number)". I chose that wording because #4508 edits the same lines to say "twenty-one" and "I1–I21". If both said "twenty-one" identically, git would merge them silently into a count that is wrong once both land. Wording that differs forces a conflict, which whoever lands second resolves to "I1–I22". The rejected option was writing "I1–I22" now, which would claim an I21 that `main` does not have yet.
- **Matching a listed pick to its declaration.** I used `play_choices::targeting_decls_of`, the reducer's own per-pick reading, rather than the plan's hand-built split with `selections_per_declaration`. It does the same job in one call.
- **Record only while the monitor's window is open,** and keep the state of each draw. The rejected option was an always-on record judged on the state after the step: it would grow without bound under the gate and AI search, and could misjudge a step that changes its own target.
- **Strict reading of the acceptance criterion.** `targeting_decls_of` uses the engine's offer lists internally, but only to decide which declaration a listed pick belongs to. Whether a pick is barred is judged only by I22's own reading. If you read the criterion strictly, this is the one place the check touches a filter's output.

## Worth a second look
- `source_barred` copies two type readings on purpose. Evasive reads the source as R781001 does: a card in a unit zone is a Unit, otherwise its printed face type. Immune to Spells reads `faces::card_type_of`, where a Spell set face-down counts as a Trap.
- The check is lenient where the engine is stricter: it does not read a face-down card's Immune to Spells. It can miss that case but cannot raise a false failure.
- I22 does not run on I14's branches, and listings under a Mayor are skipped (its plays name no targets); the record judges those draws instead.
- The open-prompt check reads the board at the sampled state. If a card turned Evasive while a Spell's prompt was already open, I22 would flag it. That never happened in 200 + 50 seeds. If the daily waves find it lawful, it goes on I22's list with its ruling.

# #4540: Patch: the fuzz monitor fails a game in which a target drawn at random is one its card could not have chosen by hand
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Some cards make their choices at random. A spell cast at random picks its own targets, and while a certain Unit is on the field every target is drawn at random. The rules say a random draw may land only on a card a player could have picked by hand, so a spell must never land on a Unit that spells can't target. A bug of exactly this kind was fixed two days ago: random casts were stealing or hitting such Units, or wasting a pick on one and doing nothing. The fuzz plays thousands of random games every day and never saw it, because a wasted pick leaves no trace in the game's record. Once this is built, the fuzz checks every random target pick against the targeting rules. The next bug of this kind, in any card, is then caught by the daily run instead of by a player.

## Why
- R452 (`spec/rulings/R0452.md`, its last sentence) says a random cast's `target` prompt draws only from the options the targeting point leaves. So it never picks an Evasive card in play (R4353002), a Unit Immune to Spells or a Dormant card (R1839000). R4353002 and R1200 say the same of a Mayor's random declared targets.
- #4500 (`f5a5cc1ffa`, 2026-11-22) fixed `cast_prompt_shape` (`crates/engine/src/prompts.rs:1292`), which answered a random cast's prompts from options nobody had filtered. Hand-built tests found the bug: `r4353002_random_cast_never_picks_evasive_enemy_unit` and `r452_random_cast_never_picks_immune_to_spells_unit_or_dormant_unit`, at `crates/engine/tests/rules/effects_cast.rs:1010` and `:1060`. The fuzz did not.
- No invariant can see such a pick today:
  - `answer_at_random` (`prompts.rs:1364`) emits nothing; its comment says 'Nothing is emitted, since no prompt was open'.
  - A declared target drawn at random goes straight into the run's targets: `random_targets::draw_picks` at `play_steps.rs:2511`, `cry_trigger.rs:339` and `play_choices.rs:2404`, and `random_picks` at `play_steps.rs:2527` and `cry_trigger.rs:367`.
  - The twenty checks in `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` never read Evasive or Immune to Spells as targeting. A grep for `evasive_bars` or `immune_to_spells` there finds nothing; Evasive appears only in I17's Defense half.
  - I8 and I14 compare `legal_actions` with `reduce`. Both ask the same filter, so a bug in the filter passes both checks.
  - I19 sees a Dormant card only when an event changes it, and a pick that the effect then skips changes nothing.
- #4508 (open) checks what a Spell changes on a Unit Immune to Spells, read from its events. This one checks what a target draw aims at, including the picks that change nothing and the Evasive half. The two do not overlap.

## Proposal
Add I21 to the invariant monitor: every `target` pick is one its source may aim at.
1. A testkit seam records each random `target` draw: the source card, the seat and the picks. It records at `answer_at_random` and at the declared-target draw sites above. It follows the thread-local pattern of `crates/engine/src/testkit/seams.rs`, which the engine consults only under `#[cfg(feature = "testkit")]`.
2. `InvariantMonitor::after` drains the record and judges each pick on its own reading of the state, as I17 does. It does not call `restrictions::evasive_bars`, `immune_to_spells` or the prompt filter (the monitor's header: an oracle, not the fix restated). It flags:
   - an Evasive card face-up on the field, when the source is a Spell or a Field Spell;
   - a Unit Immune to Spells, when the source is a Spell;
   - a Dormant card, whatever the source.
3. The same judgement applies to every `target` declaration `legal_actions` lists and every open `target` prompt's options, read in `hidden` beside I13 and I15. That catches a filter bug the listing and the reducer share.
4. Random picks made by an effect, not a targeting step, are not judged. 'A random enemy' is one: R4353002 lets such a pick reach an Evasive card.
5. Each Duos duel runs the check through `DuosInvariantMonitor`, as I19 does.

## Where it lands
- `crates/engine/src/testkit/invariants.rs` (I21 and the header's list of checks) and `crates/engine/src/testkit/seams.rs` (the record)
- `crates/engine/src/prompts.rs`, `random_targets.rs`, `play_steps.rs`, `cry_trigger.rs` and `play_choices.rs`: one testkit-only record call each
- `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs` (the tests) and `crates/tools/README.md`'s `fuzz` row
- SPEC §10.7 (the fuzz); R452, R1200, R4353002, R1839000

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] I21 fails a step whose random `target` draw names a card its source may not aim at: an Evasive card in play from a Spell or Field Spell source, a Unit Immune to Spells from a Spell source, or a Dormant card. This covers a random cast's prompt (R452) and a Mayor's declared target or prompt (R1200). The message leads with `I21`, cites the ruling and names the source and the pick.
- [ ] I21 also fails a listed `target` declaration or an open `target` prompt option that offers such a card.
- [ ] The check reads keywords, zones and face-down state itself and calls none of the engine's targeting filters.
- [ ] Tests in `crates/engine/tests/rules/invariants.rs` hand the check one bad pick of each kind and see it flagged. They also see these clean: a legal pick, a Unit or Trap source aiming at an Evasive card, and a random pick made by an effect.
- [ ] The seam and its record calls compile only under `testkit`, and `RULE_4_STATICS` in `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs` passes unchanged.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200` and `cargo jackioh fuzz --duos --seeds 50` run clean. Any breach they find is fixed in the same pull request, or filed as its own issue and named in the report.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' invariants`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

## Size and risks
Hard (engine testkit, CLAUDE.md rule 11): about 250 to 350 lines with tests, across about eight files. The seam adds a testkit-only line at about five engine sites; a release build does not change. The daily 10,000-seed waves may go red at first on a card that still draws a pick it may not. That is the point, but each such breach needs its own fix. If a lawful exception turns up, it goes on I21's list with the ruling that allows it, as I19 keeps its own.

struct PickBars { dormant: bool, evasive: bool, immune: bool }

/// R1487000, R4353002: a Trap or Field Trap (a set card among them) neither flipped nor revealed.
fn face_down_now(state: &GameState, card: &CardInstance) -> bool {
    matches!(crate::faces::card_type_of(state, card), CardType::Trap | CardType::FieldTrap)
        && card.face_up != Some(true)
        && card.revealed != Some(true)
}

fn pick_bars(state: &GameState, auras: &AuraTable<'_>, pick: &Selection) -> Option<PickBars> {
    let Selection::Instance { instance_id } = pick else { return None };
    let card = find_instance(state, instance_id)?;
    if !matches!(card.zone, Zone::Field { .. }) { return None; }
    let face_up = !face_down_now(state, card);
    let bars = PickBars {
        dormant: card.slumber.is_some(),
        evasive: face_up && auras.unit_has(card, KeywordKind::Evasive),
        immune: face_up && auras.unit_has(card, KeywordKind::ImmuneToSpells),
    };
    (bars.dormant || bars.evasive || bars.immune).then_some(bars)
}

/// Evasive reads the source as R781001 does; Immune to Spells as `faces::card_type_of` (R450).
fn source_barred(state: &GameState, source: Option<&CardInstance>, bars: &PickBars) -> Option<(&'static str, &'static str)> {
    if bars.dormant { return Some(("a Dormant card, which nothing targets", "R1839000")); }
    let source = source?;
    let aims_as = match source.zone {
        Zone::Field { row: Row::Units, .. } => CardType::Unit,
        _ => crate::faces::card_type_of_face(state, &source.def_id, source.radiant),
    };
    if bars.evasive && matches!(aims_as, CardType::Spell | CardType::FieldSpell) {
        return Some(("an Evasive card in play, which no Spell or Field Spell targets", "R4353002"));
    }
    if bars.immune && crate::faces::card_type_of(state, source) == CardType::Spell {
        return Some(("a card Immune to Spells, which no Spell targets", "R450"));
    }
    None
}
```

     - For an Activate, the source is the card and the declarations are the `targets` of the `subsystems::activate::abilities_of` entry whose `id` is `ability` (the first entry when `None`).
     - Split with `selections_per_declaration(state, viewer, &source, &active_target_decls(&decls, &modes), targets)`, the reducer's own split.
     - Judge the barred picks in `PromptKind::Target` slices.
     - Message: `I21 unlawful listed target: {viewer}'s {play|activation} of {name_of(source)} offers {pick} on turn {turn}: {what} ({rule})`.
   - `offered_target_findings(state: &GameState) -> Vec<String>`

struct PickBars { dormant: bool, evasive: bool, immune: bool }

/// R1487000, R4353002: a Trap or Field Trap (a set card among them) neither flipped nor revealed.
fn face_down_now(state: &GameState, card: &CardInstance) -> bool {
    matches!(crate::faces::card_type_of(state, card), CardType::Trap | CardType::FieldTrap)
        && card.face_up != Some(true)
        && card.revealed != Some(true)
}

fn pick_bars(state: &GameState, auras: &AuraTable<'_>, pick: &Selection) -> Option<PickBars> {
    let Selection::Instance { instance_id } = pick else { return None };
    let card = find_instance(state, instance_id)?;
    if !matches!(card.zone, Zone::Field { .. }) { return None; }
    let face_up = !face_down_now(state, card);
    let bars = PickBars {
        dormant: card.slumber.is_some(),
        evasive: face_up && auras.unit_has(card, KeywordKind::Evasive),
        immune: face_up && auras.unit_has(card, KeywordKind::ImmuneToSpells),
    };
    (bars.dormant || bars.evasive || bars.immune).then_some(bars)
}

/// Evasive reads the source as R781001 does; Immune to Spells as `faces::card_type_of` (R450).
fn source_barred(state: &GameState, source: Option<&CardInstance>, bars: &PickBars) -> Option<(&'static str, &'static str)> {
    if bars.dormant { return Some(("a Dormant card, which nothing targets", "R1839000")); }
    let source = source?;
    let aims_as = match source.zone {
        Zone::Field { row: Row::Units, .. } => CardType::Unit,
        _ => crate::faces::card_type_of_face(state, &source.def_id, source.radiant),
    };
    if bars.evasive && matches!(aims_as, CardType::Spell | CardType::FieldSpell) {
        return Some(("an Evasive card in play, which no Spell or Field Spell targets", "R4353002"));
    }
    if bars.immune && crate::faces::card_type_of(state, source) == CardType::Spell {
        return Some(("a card Immune to Spells, which no Spell targets", "R450"));
    }
    None
}
